characteristics: AMT variant adds modern optics/comms over base T-72
Strength: Widely available across donor nations (Poland, Czechia); simple, well-understood platform
Limitation: Autoloader carousel is a known catastrophic-loss vulnerability (turret-toss) if ammo cooks off; less armor than Western types
Estimated quantity available: Pre-war ~86 T-72AV/B1 + T-72AMT organic; hundreds more via Polish/Czech donation programs (exact totals not fully disclosed)
employment_notes: Bridges the gap between depleting T-64 stock and arriving Western tanks; donated T-72 variants (many upgraded to NATO-adjacent standards) became a major share of the fleet by 2023-2024
contrast_vs_traditional: The T-72's original doctrine role was a mass-produced breakthrough tank, cheap enough to lose in quantity. The AMT package — added ERA, jammers, slat cages — is a direct field response to the modern threat that actually kills tanks now: not the anti-tank guided missiles the base design was armored against, but a top-attack FPV costing a few hundred dollars, which inverts the original cost calculus the platform was built around.
